findings.summary: A value with storage is shared into every sink whose signature it has, adapted when the sink supplies more or reads less, and only a storage-less declaration is lowered per sink; the re-lowering branch no longer sees materialized storage of an adaptable shape.

A lowering that reaches its own declaration again refuses with the function's name instead of recursing until the stack overflows, for every shape the storage cannot serve (a narrower, defaulted signature among them).

The exact-share branches no longer refuse identity-carrying sinks: an adapted or shared value keeps the storage's own identity, so a same-signature callback re-queued through an array or set shares its storage too.
The wider-signature adapter and the rest-parameter adapter are one signature mapping and one renderer, covering dropped extras, packed rest arguments and a dropped result.

The invoker's parameter is typed from the storage expression rather than a generic lambda, so make_closure takes its function-pointer path (58 to 224 KB less object code per fixture, no lambda names in RTTI).
The stored signature is a real function data type built from the value, without a cast or an ad-hoc shape; the guard conditions live in the mapping once.
The data-value equality branch the identity-insensitive branch already subsumed is gone.

The plain-realm fixture materializes the supplied-prefix case by a direct call and pins the same-signature identity sink and the dropped result; the worker-realm fixture stays as the regression for the realm that overflowed; a refusal test pins the narrower shape; the feature row states the general rule and the narrower limit.
An adapted value is rebuilt at each reach (one gc-shared body per frame for a self-scheduling frame callback) where one adapter per storage and sink signature would do.
findings.blockedBy: Hoisting one adapter beside the storage's owner needs a declaration flushed ahead of the closure line while that closure's body is still being captured, a mechanism the emitter does not have; the per-frame cost has not been measured in a frame loop.
findings.filedIn: docs/features.md (Functions limits: an adapted value is rebuilt at each reach)
